mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate signals tightening monetary policy, which raises discount rates applied to equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the CPIAUCSL index above 260.0 signals accelerating inflation, prompting central banks to raise interest rates, which compresses equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 260.0 in the next month
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns when CPIAUCSL crosses above 260.0, contradicting the expected negative signal.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in quarterly demand (GDPC1) and decline in federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS) creates a favorable macroeconomic environment, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 rises > 5% and FEDFUNDS falls > 0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: The interaction of GDPC1 and FEDFUNDS does not consistently predict positive returns over 5-day horizons, with p-values >0.05 in 30% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% in a late-cycle expansion signals strong labor market conditions, fostering corporate optimism and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 5.0% in the current regime (late-cycle expansion)
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion regimes, UNRATE falling below 5.0% does not correlate with positive 20-day returns, as per t-test p >0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Sustained monthly increases in labor employment (PAYEMS) signal strong labor demand, boosting corporate earnings expectations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: PAYEMS increases do not consistently lead to positive 5-day S&P 500 returns, with p-values >0.05 in 50% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Combined monthly rises in labor employment (PAYEMS) and demand (GDPC1) above threshold levels create a virtuous cycle of economic activity, enhancing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises > 5,000 and GDPC1 rises > 1,000 in the same month
failure_condition: The combined effect of PAYEMS and GDPC1 rises fails to predict positive 60-day returns, with p-values >0.05 in 40% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the supply index (INDPRO) below 100.0 signals weakening production capacity, leading to potential inflationary pressures and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls below 100.0 in the next month
failure_condition: INDPRO falling below 100.0 does not consistently result in negative 5-day returns, as p-values >0.05 in 60% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle, a sustained rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals aggressive policy tightening, which reduces corporate investment and equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 4.5% in the current regime (monetary tightening cycle)
failure_condition: In monetary tightening cycles, FEDFUNDS rising above 4.5% does not correlate with negative 20-day returns, p >0.05.
